name: waveform-scrub

frames.best_why: The playhead sits mid-waveform with the played bars darkened, and the name and 13 seconds remaining are clear.

tagline: An audio waveform with a draggable pin that fills bars as it plays.
summary: A compact audio card with a play button, file name and remaining time above a bar waveform. A white pin can be dragged to scrub, and the bars behind it darken as the track plays.
appearance: A dark rounded card holds a small play icon, the file name and a seconds count. Below sits a pale inner panel of thin grey vertical bars with a white pin on a long stem marking the position.
behaviour: Pressing play advances the pin and darkens the bars it passes while the seconds count down. Dragging the pin pauses playback and scrubs to that point; at the end the button becomes a replay icon.
demo_content: Standup notes with a 24 second recording and a dictated waveform
search_phrases: scrub through a recording by hand
drag the pin to seek audio
waveform that fills as it plays
use_when: A short recording such as a voice memo or clip needs visible progress and easy scrubbing in a small card.
avoid_when: Long tracks or precise seeking, since the playhead steps in tenths of a second and the bars carry no timestamps.
customise: Duration, file name and the bar height array are props; colours, the pin shape and the card radius are fixed in Tailwind classes.
weight_why: A few dozen bar divs and a 100ms interval that only runs while playing.

a11y.note: The icon play button has no accessible name or focus ring, and the playhead can only be dragged with a pointer; no reduced-motion check.

issues: The play button is an unlabelled icon with no focus ring.
The bars carry no time labels, so seeking to an exact moment is guesswork.
polish_why: Tidy compact player with a clear playhead; the plain bars and unnamed icon keep it ordinary.
